title: Muscle Length Testing — Thomas, Ely, Ober, Straight-Leg Raise and the Calf

hook.en: "Tight hamstrings" is the most over-used diagnosis in physiotherapy. Learn to test muscle length so carefully that you know which muscle is short, which compensation is hiding it and when stretching is the wrong answer.
hook.ur: “Tight hamstrings” physiotherapy ki sab se zyada istemal hone wali tashkhees hai. Muscle length itni ehtiyat se test karna seekhein ke aap ko pata ho kaun sa muscle chhota hai, kaun si compensation usay chhupa rahi hai aur stretching kab ghalat jawab hai.

goal.en: By the end, you'll perform the modified Thomas, Ely, Ober, passive straight-leg raise and gastrocnemius–soleus tests, name the normal finding and the compensation for each, and decide when stretching is justified.
goal.ur: End tak aap modified Thomas, Ely, Ober, passive straight-leg raise aur gastrocnemius–soleus tests karenge, har ek ki normal finding aur compensation batayenge, aur tay karenge ke stretching kab durust hai.

text.en: Muscle length tests move a joint **passively** until the muscle stops the movement, then ask: *is that a muscle, a joint or a nerve?* A **two-joint muscle** is only fully stretched when **both** joints are in position (rectus femoris across hip extension **and** knee flexion). A **one-joint muscle** (iliopsoas, soleus) stretches by moving only one joint. Always stop at the **first firm resistance** or the **first compensation**, whichever comes first.
text.ur: Muscle length tests joint ko **passively** tab tak hilate hain jab tak muscle movement rok de, phir poochte hain: *yeh muscle hai, joint hai ya nerve?* **Do-joint muscle** tabhi poora stretch hota hai jab **dono** joints position mein hon (rectus femoris hip extension **aur** knee flexion ke across). **Ek-joint muscle** (iliopsoas, soleus) sirf ek joint hila kar stretch hota hai. Hamesha **pehli firm resistance** ya **pehli compensation** par ruk jayein, jo bhi pehle aaye.

text.en: A short muscle is like a rubber band that is too short for its job: when you stretch it past its limit it starts pulling on whatever it is attached to. If the pelvis tilts, the back arches or the opposite leg lifts, the band has already reached its limit and is pulling the rest of the body along. That tilt is your signal to stop and read the angle.
text.ur: Chhota muscle aisi rabar band hai jo apne kaam ke liye bohat chhoti ho: aap isay us ki hadd se zyada kheenchein to woh jis se jura hai usay kheenchna shuru kar deti hai. Agar pelvis tilt ho, kamar arch ho ya doosri taang uth jaye to band apni hadd tak pohnch chuki hai aur baqi jism ko saath kheench rahi hai. Yeh tilt rukne aur angle parhne ka ishara hai.

intro.en: Lying at the end of the plinth, the patient holds the opposite knee to the chest to flatten the lumbar spine while the test leg hangs. Look for the thigh staying **above the plinth** (iliopsoas tight), the knee extended less than about 80° of flexion (rectus femoris tight) and the thigh drifting outward (TFL / ITB).
intro.ur: Plinth ke end par lete hue patient opposite knee ko seene se laga kar lumbar spine ko chapta karta hai jabke test wali taang latki rehti hai. Dekhein: thigh **plinth se upar** rahe (iliopsoas tight), knee takriban 80° flexion se kam (rectus femoris tight), thigh bahar ki taraf drift (TFL / ITB).

question.en: In the modified Thomas test the thigh lifts off the plinth but the knee angle is normal. Which muscle is short?
question.ur: Modified Thomas test mein thigh plinth se uth jati hai lekin knee ka angle normal hai. Kaun sa muscle chhota hai?

feedback.en: Yes — the thigh stays up because the hip cannot reach extension; a normal knee angle excludes rectus femoris.
feedback.ur: Haan — thigh isliye upar rehti hai ke hip extension tak nahi pohnch pata; normal knee angle rectus femoris ko rule out karta hai.

feedback.en: A short rectus femoris would limit knee flexion, not the thigh position.
feedback.ur: Chhota rectus femoris knee flexion ko limit karta, thigh ki position ko nahi.

feedback.en: Hamstrings are not stretched in this test.
feedback.ur: Is test mein hamstrings stretch nahi hotay.

intro.en: Prone with the pelvis flat, the examiner bends the knee toward the buttock. A short rectus femoris makes the **buttock rise** (the hip flexes) before the heel arrives. Watch the pelvis, not just the knee.
intro.ur: Prone, pelvis chapta, examiner knee ko buttock ki taraf mor'ta hai. Chhota rectus femoris heel pohnchne se pehle **buttock ko uthata** hai (hip flex hota hai). Sirf knee nahi, pelvis dekhein.

intro.en: Side-lying with the lower leg bent, the examiner abducts and slightly extends the top hip, then lets it go. The thigh should **drop below horizontal**; if it stays abducted the TFL and iliotibial band are short. A false negative happens if the hip flexes or rotates.
intro.ur: Side-lying, neeche wali taang mori hui, examiner upar wale hip ko abduct aur thora extend kar ke chhor deta hai. Thigh **horizontal se neeche** girni chahiye; abducted rahe to TFL aur iliotibial band chhote hain. Hip flex ya rotate ho jaye to false negative aata hai.

intro.en: Supine with the opposite leg flat, the examiner lifts the straight leg until firm resistance or the pelvis begins to tilt, then measures hip flexion. About 80° or more is normal; less than 70° with a stretch at the back of the thigh suggests short hamstrings.
intro.ur: Supine, doosri taang flat, examiner seedhi taang ko firm resistance ya pelvis ke tilt hone tak uthata hai, phir hip flexion naapta hai. Takriban 80° ya zyada normal hai; 70° se kam aur thigh ke peechay stretch chhote hamstrings batata hai.

rows.en: Thigh rests on the plinth, knee flexed about 80–90°, thigh in neutral
rows.ur: Thigh plinth par, knee takriban 80–90° flexed, thigh neutral

rows.en: Thigh up = iliopsoas; knee less than 80° = rectus femoris; thigh abducts = TFL/ITB
rows.ur: Thigh upar = iliopsoas; knee 80° se kam = rectus femoris; thigh abduct = TFL/ITB

rows.en: Heel nearly reaches the buttock with the pelvis flat
rows.ur: Heel buttock ke qareeb, pelvis chapta

rows.en: Buttock rises or the hip flexes = short rectus femoris
rows.ur: Buttock uthe ya hip flex ho = chhota rectus femoris

rows.en: Thigh stays abducted = short TFL/ITB (check the hip did not flex or rotate)
rows.ur: Thigh abducted rahe = chhota TFL/ITB (check karein hip flex ya rotate na hua ho)

rows.en: About 80° or more hip flexion before firm resistance
rows.ur: Firm resistance se pehle takriban 80° ya zyada hip flexion

rows.en: Below about 70° with stretch at the back of the thigh = short hamstrings
rows.ur: Takriban 70° se kam aur thigh ke peechay stretch = chhote hamstrings

text.en: **Over-pulling the opposite knee.** In the Thomas test, pulling the opposite knee too far tilts the pelvis backwards and makes the hip flexors look **tighter** than they are; pulling too little leaves the lumbar spine extended and **hides** the tightness. Hold the opposite knee just enough to flatten the lower back. In the SLR, allowing the knee to bend or the opposite thigh to lift measures the wrong thing. Watch the ASIS, not only the angle.
text.ur: **Opposite knee ko zyada kheenchna.** Thomas test mein opposite knee ko zyada kheenchne se pelvis peechay tilt hota hai aur hip flexors asal se **zyada tight** lagte hain; kam kheenchne se lumbar spine extended rehti hai aur tightness **chhup** jati hai. Opposite knee ko bas itna pakrein ke neechli kamar chapti ho. SLR mein knee ko mor'ne ya opposite thigh ko uthne dena galat cheez naapta hai. Sirf angle nahi, ASIS dekhein.

question.en: Which finding means the **gastrocnemius** (not the soleus) is short?
question.ur: Kaun si finding batati hai ke **gastrocnemius** (soleus nahi) chhota hai?

text.en: Dorsiflexion is limited with the knee straight but improves a lot with the knee bent
text.ur: Dorsiflexion knee seedha ho to limited lekin knee mora ho to bohat behtar

feedback.en: Yes — bending the knee slackens the gastrocnemius; whatever remains limited belongs to the soleus or the ankle joint.
feedback.ur: Haan — knee mor'ne se gastrocnemius dheela hota hai; jo rukawat baqi rahe woh soleus ya ankle joint ki hai.

text.en: Dorsiflexion is equally limited with the knee straight and bent
text.ur: Dorsiflexion knee seedha aur mora dono mein barabar limited

feedback.en: That points to the soleus or the ankle joint.
feedback.ur: Yeh soleus ya ankle joint ki taraf ishara hai.

text.en: **Do not stretch every short muscle.** Treat a short muscle only if it matters to the problem. Static stretching of 15–30 seconds, 2–4 repeats, most days, for at least 6 weeks changes muscle range; strengthen the lengthened antagonist at the same time; and **re-test with the same test** to prove the change. Typical pairings: short hip flexors + weak glutes → stretch and glute strengthening; short pectoralis minor + shoulder pain → stretch plus lower trapezius and serratus work. Spasticity is not shortness; manage tone first.
text.ur: **Har chhote muscle ko stretch na karein.** Chhote muscle ka ilaaj tabhi karein jab woh masle se jura ho. 15–30 seconds ki static stretching, 2–4 repeats, aksar dinon mein, kam az kam 6 haftay muscle ki range badalti hai; saath hi lambay hue antagonist ko strengthen karein; aur change saabit karne ke liye **wohi test dobara** karein. Aam jore: chhote hip flexors + kamzor glutes → stretch aur glute strengthening; chhota pectoralis minor + shoulder pain → stretch aur lower trapezius aur serratus kaam. Spasticity shortness nahi hai; pehle tone manage karein.

text.en: Muscle length tests are **moderately reliable** and their validity is limited: the Thomas test shows good reliability for the hip flexors, the Ober test is influenced by many factors and is **not specific** for the iliotibial band (the band cannot be lengthened much by stretching), and the passive SLR is a better measure of nerve mobility plus hamstring extensibility together. Hamstring "tightness" is often **stretch tolerance** rather than a short muscle: range improves after stretching mainly because tolerance rises.
text.ur: Muscle length tests **moderately reliable** hain aur unki validity mahdood hai: Thomas test hip flexors ke liye achi reliability dikhata hai, Ober test par kayi cheezein asar daalti hain aur yeh iliotibial band ke liye **specific nahi** hai (band ko stretching se zyada lamba nahi kiya ja sakta), aur passive SLR nerve mobility aur hamstring extensibility dono ko saath naapta hai. Hamstring “tightness” aksar chhote muscle ke bajaye **stretch tolerance** hoti hai: stretching ke baad range isliye barhti hai ke tolerance barhti hai.

question.en: The straight-leg raise reproduces posterior-thigh pain at 50°, and adding ankle dorsiflexion makes it worse. Is this a short hamstring?
question.ur: Straight-leg raise 50° par thigh ke peechay dard reproduce karta hai, aur ankle dorsiflexion add karne se barh jata hai. Kya yeh chhota hamstring hai?

answer.en: Probably not. Dorsiflexion lengthens the **sciatic nerve** but not the hamstring. If symptoms change with dorsiflexion (or neck flexion) the nerve is involved — this is **structural differentiation**. A short hamstring would not change.
answer.ur: Shayad nahi. Dorsiflexion **sciatic nerve** ko lamba karti hai magar hamstring ko nahi. Agar dorsiflexion (ya neck flexion) se symptoms badlein to nerve involved hai — yeh **structural differentiation** hai. Chhote hamstring mein tabdeeli nahi hoti.

question.en: Which end-feel suggests a short muscle rather than a joint block?
question.ur: Kaun si end-feel chhote muscle ki taraf ishara karti hai, joint block ki nahi?

text.en: Firm and slightly elastic, with the stretch felt in the muscle
text.ur: Firm aur halki elastic, stretch muscle mein mehsoos

feedback.en: Yes — a hard, abrupt end-feel suggests bone or joint, and empty means pain stops you first.
feedback.ur: Haan — sakht, achanak end-feel haddi ya joint ki taraf ishara karti hai, aur empty ka matlab dard pehle rok deta hai.

text.en: Empty — pain stops you before resistance
text.ur: Empty — dard resistance se pehle rok de

feedback.en: That suggests serious pathology or severe irritability.
feedback.ur: Yeh serious pathology ya shadeed irritability ki taraf ishara hai.

text.en: **Refer** instead of stretching if the limited range comes with a hot swollen joint, fever, a recent fracture or surgery, unexplained night pain or weight loss (infection or malignancy), or neurological signs. Screen for hypermobility (Beighton score 5/9 or more) before stretching anyone; stretching a hypermobile person can do harm.
text.ur: Stretch karne ke bajaye **refer karein** agar mehdood range ke saath garam sooja joint, bukhar, haali fracture ya surgery, be-wajah raat ka dard ya wazan ghatna (infection ya malignancy), ya neurological signs hon. Kisi ko bhi stretch karne se pehle hypermobility screen karein (Beighton score 5/9 ya zyada); hypermobile shakhs ko stretch karna nuksan kar sakta hai.

summary.en: Move passively to the first firm resistance or compensation; two-joint muscles need both joints in position, one-joint muscles need only one.
summary.ur: Pehli firm resistance ya compensation tak passively move karein; do-joint muscles ko dono joints position mein chahiye, ek-joint muscles ko sirf ek.

summary.en: Know the four tests: Thomas (hip flexors), Ely (rectus femoris), Ober (TFL/ITB), passive SLR (hamstrings), and the calf with the knee straight or bent.
summary.ur: Chaar tests jaanein: Thomas (hip flexors), Ely (rectus femoris), Ober (TFL/ITB), passive SLR (hamstrings), aur calf knee seedha ya mora hua.

summary.en: Stretch only if the short muscle matters; separate muscle from nerve with structural differentiation; screen for hypermobility first.
summary.ur: Stretch tabhi karein jab chhota muscle masle se jura ho; structural differentiation se muscle ko nerve se alag karein; pehle hypermobility screen karein.

front.en: What does the modified Thomas test assess?
front.ur: Modified Thomas test kya assess karta hai?

back.en: The length of the hip flexors: iliopsoas (thigh up), rectus femoris (knee flexion under 80°) and TFL/ITB (thigh drifts out).
back.ur: Hip flexors ki length: iliopsoas (thigh upar), rectus femoris (knee flexion 80° se kam) aur TFL/ITB (thigh bahar).

back.en: The buttock rises or the hip flexes as the knee is bent: a short rectus femoris.
back.ur: Knee mor'te waqt buttock uthe ya hip flex ho: chhota rectus femoris.

back.en: About 80° or more of hip flexion with the knee straight.
back.ur: Knee seedha rakh kar takriban 80° ya zyada hip flexion.

front.en: How do you separate gastrocnemius from soleus tightness?
front.ur: Gastrocnemius ko soleus ki tightness se kaise alag karte hain?

back.en: Measure dorsiflexion with the knee straight and bent: limited only when straight = gastrocnemius.
back.ur: Dorsiflexion knee seedha aur mora dono mein naapein: sirf seedhe mein limited = gastrocnemius.

goDeeper.title: Muscle length skill in the Skills Lab

note.en: Watch every muscle length test in 3D and check the compensation.
note.ur: Har muscle length test 3D mein dekhein aur compensation check karein.
Do-joint muscles mukhtalif kyun behave karte hain.
